o1.biggest_strength: It leads with a blunt answer (we lose on agency reporting, not data quality) and quantifies that Lite usage-limit exits are 32% of all churn — 1.6% of paying customers a month — then puts a stop-list and a don't-spend list beside the five moves.
o1.biggest_mistake: Move 5 (free Monday report inside AWT) partly duplicates moves 1 and 3, so one of the five slots is spent on a variant rather than an independent bet.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the overlapping fifth move with something independent — for example a Lite-to-Standard step-pricing test aimed squarely at the in-house 'price jump' complaint — and give each move a revenue estimate or state plainly why it can't be sized.

o2.biggest_strength: The trial-loss working (27 trials x 89% x 54% = 13.0 per 100, and winning back a quarter lifts conversions from 16.7 to 19.9) is tight and traceable, and interviewing 20 lost agencies before speccing the report is a genuinely cheap first step.
o2.biggest_mistake: Move 5, 'teach with our link data', is the 'do more content' advice I explicitly didn't want; its success metric (in-house share of trials rising above 38%) has no credible causal link to publishing one study.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap move 5 for a move that acts on a number in the data — the Lite-to-Standard price step or an Advanced save-play against the 28% Semrush exits — and set real target deltas, not just 'rises above today's figure'.

reason: Both get the core call right — fight on agency reporting, refuse PPC parity, fix Lite limits — but Output 1 says it faster, tells me what to stop and not spend on, and its fifth move is an idea I hadn't had, while Output 2's fifth move is the generic content advice I warned against.
